headline: Underwriting profit climbs while investment swings cut EPS

kpis.label: Adjusted after-tax income per diluted share (AATI)

summary_short: AIG's Q2 FY2026 net premiums written rose 9% y/y to $7.5 billion and General Insurance underwriting income grew 10% to $686 million, but GAAP diluted EPS fell 10.1% y/y to $1.78 on investment-related fair-value swings tied to its Corebridge exit; adjusted (AATI) diluted EPS rose 10.5% to $2.00.
summary_long: General Insurance NPW grew 9% y/y to $7.5 billion, with underwriting income up 10% to $686 million and the combined ratio improving 30bp to 89.0%. GAAP net income fell 10% y/y to $948 million ($1.78/diluted share) on mark-to-market swings in AIG's former Corebridge stake and equity securities, partially offset by higher underwriting income; AATI rose 10% to $1.07 billion ($2.00/diluted share). AIG completed its Corebridge exit in May for ~$710 million and returned $904 million to shareholders via $641 million of buybacks and $263 million of dividends. Shareholders' equity fell 2.2% y/y to $40.6 billion even as book value per share rose 4.4% to $77.39 on the reduced share count. No numeric guidance was issued this quarter.

drivers.metric: Adjusted after-tax income per diluted share (AATI)
drivers.explanation: Increase reflects higher underwriting income, partially offset by lower Other Operations net investment income.
Improvement driven by higher favorable prior-year reserve development and a lower expense ratio, partially offset by higher catastrophe-related charges.
Growth driven by organic growth across all three business segments and recent strategic transactions, partially offset by declines in North America Property lines.
Rose y/y even as total shareholders' equity fell, because the buyback-driven drop in shares outstanding (559.8M to 524.7M) outpaced the equity decline.

Management cites an 'exceptional first half,' with organic growth and strategic transactions offsetting a more selective pricing environment; reiterated confidence in 2025 Investor Day objectives without new numeric guidance.
